title: The binomial row sum is a power of two
statement: For every natural n, the sum of the n-th row of Pascal's triangle is 2^n: sum over all integers k of C(n,k) equals 2^n. The summand vanishes outside 0 <= k <= n, so the sum is finite.

formal.statement:
(define-hyperterm F (* (gamma (+ n 1)) (/ 1 (gamma (+ k 1))) (/ 1 (gamma (+ (- n k) 1)))))
(define-hyperterm T (^ 2 n))
(assert (forall ((n Int)) (=> (>= n 0) (= (sum ((k Int)) F) T))))

evidence.supports: the creative-telescoping certificate, replayed by a checker that shares no code with the search that produced it
checkers: telescoping_check::confirm_ratios (shift ratios against exact bignum factorials)
telescoping_check::confirm_telescoping (pointwise identity and summed recurrence, exact bignum)
evidence.notes: Certificate: order 1, recurrence coefficients a_0 = 2, a_1 = -1 (i.e. S(n+1) = 2*S(n)), R(n,k) = k / (n - k + 1). Closed form 2^n verified to satisfy the same recurrence (a rational-function identity in its own shift ratio); base case S(0) = 1 = 2^0 checked by exact summation; leading coefficient a_1 = -1 has no integer zero, so the recurrence runs forward from n = 0.

notes: Established on the `cas-certificate` route: an untrusted linear-algebra search (axeyum_cas::telescoping::zeilberger) produced the certificate, and axeyum_cas::telescoping_check verified it with its own shift-ratio derivation, its own fraction arithmetic, and a cross-check of both against exact bignum factorial evaluation of the summand. The checker rejects perturbed certificates -- see the tamper controls in the same test file (P+1, 2P, Q+k, a wrong recurrence constant, a degree bump in a_j, a zeroed recurrence, a certificate re-pointed at a different summand, a clipped summation window, and two wrong closed forms are all rejected).
